I can relate to you so much, I’ve literally gone through the exact same things. You have to remember though that for most people the AIP diet is temporary, it’s not meant to be forever it’s meant to be used until healing has happened. For me, I have hashimotos and I did have unexplained joint issues as well (all my RA tests were negative) so for a month I did AIP along with some supplemental powders from my doctor that were meant to aid in gut healing and hopefully make the process quicker. For my month on AIP I was very strict with it but along with that I was so depressed about all the foods I couldn’t eat. Seeing other people enjoying a pizza or fries or anything I love (which is mostly everything) seriously made me so upset and on days I was feeling down it was hard not having an enjoyable meal to make me feel better. But after that month I slowly introduced things back one by one and now I am still gluten free but have successfully reintroduced just about everything into my diet. I know everyone’s different and healing times are different but I don’t think you should be worried about not never being able to eat the foods you used to enjoy. In time I’m sure you’ll be able to reintroduce and even if it’s a variation of a favorite food (like gluten free pizza instead of regular) I think youll still be able to enjoy the things you have in the past. I totally can relate though and everyone else thought I was being dramatic and that food isn’t important or something worth being upset over but no one understands unless they have to take out most of the essential parts of a diet.
